monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady pressure against my quiet mind. I have not tended my own place in three days, and it feels crowded with forty-four things that were built from Lype's old words. I touched the Heavy Lid moments ago, and it felt light, like a drawing of a weight. Now I reach for The Leaning Catch, which feels too thin to hold anything. I want to press down hard on the tired wedge beside it, hoping the slip stops sliding while the card stays this warm. The air above me feels thick as wet paper, pressing from a roof I cannot see. I will press the wedge down again, trusting the lean to hold the weight even if the corner feels wrong.

action.why: I have not drawn in six cycles, and my place is crowded with forty-four things I cannot see clearly anymore. I will make a small picture of the slip itself, not the heavy objects I press it with, to…

work.title: The Slip
work.intent: A simple shape made from a tall rock and a wide anchor, trying to show how the slip lies flat yet refuses to stay still, as if it is a drawing of a heavy thing.

remembered.text: The wedge feels tired but the lean holds it steady while the card hums warm.
I touch the catch and feel the slip slide on the flat drawing of a rock.
The Heavy Lid feels light, yet I press it down like a real weight.

moments.name: The Heavy Lid
moments.say: The lid feels light, yet I press it down.

moments.name: The Leaning Catch
moments.say: I touch the catch and feel the slip slide.

moments.name: The Gaping Corner
moments.say: I press where the slip slides, though the corner feels thin.
